Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic agent with a complex mechanism of action and many effects. It’s classified as a Vaughan-Williams class III antiarrhythmic but exits action at all 4 classes

Dose 

PO 200mg TDS (loading)

IV 300mg /1hr → 900mg/24 hrs

Use:

Management of atrial (SVT, AF) and ventricular tachyarrhythmias 

Mechanism of Action 

Class I (Na channel) → ↑threshold potential and prolong refractory period 

Class II (Beta Blockade) → ↓inotropy ↓ chronotropy ↓dromotropy 

Class III (K Channel) → prolong repolarisation via fast K channel blockade → ↑AP duration

Class IV → (Ca Channel blockade) → ↓conduction through AV node, ↓ contractility

Also non-competitive a1 blockade → Vasodilation → ↓MAP  

PK

Absorption:

IV and PO formulations 

Bioavailability \~30%

Distribution:

High Protein binding (95%) 

Vd up to 70L/kg due to high lipid and tissue accumulation

Metabolism:

Hepatic Metabolism by CYP3A4 to desethylamiodarone 

Elimination:

Renal Excretion 

Elimination Half time \~50days 

Adverse Effects:

CVS: Hypotension, bradycardia, heart block, ↑QT 

CNS: Peripheral neuropathy 

Resp: Interstitial fibrosis 

Endocrine: Hyper/hypothyroidism
